title: PetSmart upgraded thanks in part to Chewy IPO
summary: PetSmart's credit rating has been upgraded by Moody's Investor Service and S&P Global, partially due to the success of Chewy's initial public offering. The IPO proceeds allowed PetSmart to repay debt, improving its leverage and overall financial outlook. This upgrade comes despite an increasingly saturated pet retail market.

title: Elastic SIEM woos enterprises with cost savings
summary: Elastic SIEM is gaining interest from enterprises, especially former Splunk users, due to its promise of cost savings and its ability to centralize security analytics and IT monitoring data. The tool standardizes data schemas and offers a competitive alternative to established players like Splunk and AWS in the security analytics market. Its future integration with Endgame, an endpoint security company, is seen as a significant long-term appeal for the application.

title: GIC to Fuel Equinix’s Hyperscale Market Ambition
summary: Equinix, the world’s largest data center provider, is partnering with GIC, Singapore’s sovereign wealth fund, in a $1 billion joint venture to build and operate hyperscale data centers for major digital platforms. This initiative, branded xScale, aims to address the growing demand from tech giants like Alibaba, Amazon, and Microsoft for large-scale data center capacity, especially in Europe. The move allows Equinix to expand into the hyperscale market without cannibalizing its core retail colocation business, leveraging GIC’s capital for significant investments.

title: Interview with Thomas M. Siebel on Digital Tranformation
summary: Thomas M. Siebel, Chairman and CEO of C3.ai, discusses his entrepreneurial journey from Oracle to Siebel Systems and now C3.ai, highlighting the impact of digital transformation driven by elastic cloud computing, big data, AI, and IoT. He shares insights on building a company culture, the potential negative impacts of AI, and the thesis of his book "Digital Transformation," urging business leaders to adapt to an existential shift in the corporate world. Siebel also touches on entrepreneurial philanthropy and offers advice to young professionals.

title: In Court Filing, Prime Inc. Says Amazon’s Use of ‘Prime’ Causes Confusion
summary: Prime Inc. has filed a complaint against Amazon, alleging that Amazon’s use of "Prime" on its shipping vehicles creates a likelihood of confusion with Prime Inc.'s trucking business. Prime Inc. claims Amazon's trademark registration should be canceled due to fraud, as Amazon did not transport goods itself at the time of its 2005 application. Prime Inc. is seeking injunctive relief, damages, and attorneys' fees in addition to trademark cancellation.

title: Amazon can be held liable for third-party seller products: U.S. appeals court
summary: A federal appeals court has ruled that Amazon.com Inc can be held liable for defective products sold by third-party vendors on its platform, a decision that departs from previous court rulings. This ruling, based on Pennsylvania law, stemmed from a lawsuit filed by a customer who was injured by a retractable dog leash purchased via Amazon's website. The court highlighted that Amazon's business model can obscure third-party vendors, leaving injured customers without direct recourse.

title: Mark Shuttleworth sold a tech startup he built in his garage for $575 million and used the money to visit space
summary: Mark Shuttleworth, founder of Thawte, sold his tech startup for $575 million in 1999 and used $20 million to finance a trip to space in 2002. He later founded Canonical, an open-source software provider, which he fully funded himself. Shuttleworth details his journey from starting Thawte in his parents' garage to his space adventure and his vision for open source through Canonical.

title: Report: Amazon Founder Bezos’ Divorce Final; Settlement $38B
summary: Amazon.com Inc. founder Jeff Bezos and MacKenzie Bezos have finalized their divorce, with MacKenzie set to receive $38.3 billion in Amazon stock. Jeff Bezos will retain voting control of her shares and remains the world's richest person with a 12% stake. MacKenzie Bezos has pledged to give half of her fortune to charity as part of the "Giving Pledge."
source: VOA - Voice of America English News

title: Razer Chroma lighting comes to AMD Ryzen 7 and 9 Wraith Prism fans
summary: Razer has partnered with AMD to integrate Chroma RGB lighting into the Wraith Prism fans included with AMD's new 3rd Gen Ryzen 7 and 9 CPUs. This collaboration allows users to synchronize the lighting of their CPU cooler with other Razer Chroma accessories through the Synapse software, enhancing the aesthetic consistency of gaming setups. The 3rd Gen Ryzen 3000 Series CPUs, with prices starting at $200, are now available, though Chroma integration is exclusive to the Ryzen 7 and 9 chips.

title: Prime, Inc. trucking sues Amazon Prime for use of name
summary: Prime, Inc., a Springfield-based trucking company, is suing Amazon Prime for alleged trademark infringement. Prime, Inc. claims Amazon's use of "Prime" on its tractor-trailers causes confusion and economic loss, despite being notified over two years ago. The lawsuit seeks significant damages, arguing Amazon's infringement is "intentional, willful, and malicious."

title: Here is What You Need to Know About Douyu, Chinese Streaming Unicorn Eyeing US IPO
summary: Douyu, a leading Chinese game streaming unicorn backed by Tencent, is preparing for a US IPO with an expected valuation between $3.73 billion and $4.54 billion. The company reported a profitable Q1 2019, with revenues soaring 123.4% year-on-year and a significant increase in paying users to over 6 million, surpassing its rival Huya. Despite its success, concerns remain about Douyu's long-term growth and its reliance on user tips, differing significantly from Twitch's more diverse revenue streams.

title: Piper Jaffray announces $485M deal for Sandler O'Neill, new name
summary: Piper Jaffray Cos. announced it will acquire fellow investment bank Sandler O'Neill for $485 million. The combined entity will operate under the new name Piper Sandler Cos. Chad Abraham, CEO of Piper Jaffray, will lead the new firm.

title: Prime seeks damages in Amazon trademark dispute
summary: Springfield-based trucking and logistics company Prime Inc. is suing Amazon.com Inc. for trademark infringement, seeking damages equal to three times Amazon's profits or Prime Inc.'s losses. The lawsuit alleges customer confusion due to Amazon's use of "Prime" for its shipping services, which Prime Inc. claims to have used since 1980. Prime Inc. argues Amazon's Prime logos are "confusingly similar" and impact its reputation in the transportation sector.

title: IBM closes $34 billion deal to buy Red Hat to boost cloud business
summary: IBM has completed its $34 billion acquisition of Red Hat Inc., marking its largest-ever deal, to significantly bolster its cloud computing business. This strategic move aims to help companies transition to hybrid cloud environments, offering a mix of public and private cloud applications. Red Hat will operate as a distinct unit within IBM, maintaining its headquarters and management, with no immediate job or cost cuts planned.

title: Prime Inc. sues Amazon Prime for trademark infringement
summary: New Prime Inc., a trucking company, has filed a lawsuit against Amazon for trademark infringement, alleging that Amazon's "Prime" logos and services have caused customer confusion and harmed its business. Prime Inc. claims to have used the "Prime Inc." phrase for nearly 40 years and that Amazon falsely represented its shipping services when it sought to register the Prime word mark. The lawsuit seeks injunctive relief, actual damages, attorney's fees, and the cancellation of Amazon’s U.S. Patent and Trademark Office registration for "Prime."

title: Springfield trucking company sues Amazon over use of 'Prime'
summary: Springfield-based trucking company Prime Inc. is suing Amazon for its use of "Prime" on shipping vehicles, claiming it causes confusion and irreparable damage to its brand. Prime Inc., which has used the "Prime Inc." logo since 1980, alleges Amazon's similar "Amazon Prime" logo on tractor trailers violates federal trademark law and misleads consumers. The lawsuit argues that consumers might associate negative experiences with Amazon with Prime Inc., harming its reputation and goodwill.

title: Prime, Inc. takes Amazon to court over retailer’s use of ‘Prime’ on its trucks
summary: Prime, Inc., a Springfield, Missouri-based trucking company, has filed a lawsuit against Amazon, seeking to revoke Amazon’s "Prime" trademark and claim damages. Prime, Inc. argues that Amazon's use of "Prime" on its trucks creates public confusion and negatively impacts its reputation and bottom line. The lawsuit contends that Amazon falsely represented its services in its trademark application and that Prime, Inc. had established prior common law rights to the name since 1970.

title: Big tech company to move HQ from Sunnyvale to San Jose
summary: Rambus Inc. is relocating its headquarters from Sunnyvale to North San Jose, acquiring 90,000 square feet at 4453 North First St. The move is driven by the desire for a more modern workspace, lower lease costs, and proximity to employee housing, reflecting a broader trend of tech companies moving to San Jose as the Peninsula's commercial vacancy rates tighten. This shift highlights San Jose's growing appeal for tech companies, demonstrated by other recent moves like HPE and McAfee, and ongoing development in the area.

title: Prime, Inc. sues Amazon over trademarked "Prime" logo
summary: Prime, Inc., a trucking company, has filed a lawsuit against Amazon, alleging trademark infringement over Amazon's use of the "Prime" logo on its trucks and trailers. Prime, Inc. claims to have used its name and logo on their vehicles for over 40 years and holds the trademark for "transportation services by truck." The lawsuit seeks monetary damages and an injunction against Amazon's continued use of the logo on its trailers.

title: Prime, Inc. takes Amazon to court over use of ‘prime’ on trailers
summary: Prime, Inc., the 14th largest trucking company in the U.S., has filed a lawsuit against Amazon alleging trademark infringement over the use of the word "prime" on Amazon's trailers. Prime, Inc. claims to have used its name and logo on trucks and trailers for over 40 years and holds trademarks for "transportation services by truck." The lawsuit seeks monetary damages and an injunction against Amazon's continued use of the "Amazon Prime" logo on its trailers.

title: Cloud Volumes ONTAP: Experience the Benefits of ONTAP Across Azure, AWS, and GCP
summary: NetApp has expanded its Cloud Volumes ONTAP (CVO) offering to include Google Cloud Platform (GCP), making it available across all three major cloud providers: Microsoft Azure, Amazon AWS, and Google Cloud Platform. CVO offers full ONTAP features in the cloud, enabling use cases like multi-cloud disaster recovery, cost-efficient storage for cloud-native applications, and persistent storage for Docker and Kubernetes. The article differentiates CVO (IaaS, user-managed) from Cloud Volumes Service (CVS) (PaaS, fully managed).

title: Alexa co-creator: Digital world forgot importance of real dialogue
summary: Alex Spinelli, former global head of Alexa for Amazon and current LivePerson CTO, states that the digital world has become too focused on interfaces and has lost sight of using technology to truly connect with and understand consumers. He suggests that this focus has detracted from the original purpose of digital interaction, which should be about real dialogue.

title: Investors Use Indexes to Play in the Video Game Business (Published 2019)
summary: The video game industry, transitioning from arcades to mobile and streaming, presents significant investment opportunities. Big tech companies like Microsoft, Google, and Amazon are entering the streaming video game market, alongside equipment makers and game publishers set to capitalize on new capabilities. The industry is projected to reach $180 billion in annual sales, with investors increasingly using exchange-traded funds to gain exposure.

title: Amazon's top cardboard box makers face challenges from plastic mailers
summary: Cardboard box manufacturers, including suppliers to Amazon like Westrock and International Paper, initially benefited greatly from the boom in e-commerce, especially Amazon Prime's growing package volume. However, Amazon is now shifting towards plastic mailers and bags for smaller products to cut costs and speed up delivery, posing a new challenge for the cardboard industry. This move comes after the industry found a saving grace in e-commerce following a decline in demand for traditional paper products and the impact of the Great Recession.

title: Blackstone buys warehouse assets for $18.7bn
summary: Blackstone Group LP has acquired the US industrial warehouse properties of Singapore-based logistics provider GLP for $18.7 billion, marking the largest private real estate transaction globally. This deal significantly expands Blackstone's US industrial footprint, nearly doubling its existing assets and making it the largest US owner and operator of warehouses focused on e-commerce. The acquisition builds on Blackstone's strategy to invest in logistics as a key global investment theme, leveraging the growing demand driven by e-commerce.

title: Target launches 'tween' brand in time for back-to-school rush
summary: Target has launched a new "tween" brand called "More than Magic" just in time for the back-to-school season. This multiproduct line, designed for 9- to 13-year-old girls, includes apparel, electronics, and school supplies, with most items under $30. The move aims to capture the back-to-school market and cater to an underserved demographic as many mall-based specialty "tween" stores are closing.

title: This new business from Amazon represents a '$100 billion opportunity,' Morgan Stanley says
summary: Morgan Stanley estimates that Amazon's Project Kuiper, a planned network of 3,236 satellites to provide global high-speed internet, could represent a "$100 billion opportunity." This projection is based on the firm's expectation that the overall space economy will grow to over $1 trillion in the next 20 years. Project Kuiper positions Amazon to compete with companies like SpaceX in the race to build next-generation internet satellite networks, with analyst Adam Jonas highlighting Jeff Bezos's increasing financial commitment to space ventures through Blue Origin.

title: How Amazon Prime Day uses your psychology to get you to buy
summary: Amazon Prime Day leverages various psychological tactics to encourage purchases, transforming a simple sale into a major shopping holiday. Key strategies include creating exclusivity for Prime members, employing scarcity and urgency through limited-time deals and countdown clocks, and fostering a viral social media environment. While effective, these tactics can lead to buyer's remorse or "inaction inertia" if consumers miss out on deals and later devalue products at regular prices.

title: Milwaukee seeks to expand Century City Business Park -- even as it struggles to attract north side development
summary: The City of Milwaukee plans to expand its Century City Business Park by purchasing 13.7 acres for $250,000, despite previous difficulties attracting development. The expansion aims to increase visibility with more Capitol Drive frontage and provide additional space, making it more attractive to potential businesses. While the city has invested significantly in the park, it has struggled to secure tenants, with several large companies opting for other locations.

title: Disney Content Sales President Janice Marinelli to Depart
summary: Janice Marinelli, President of global sales and marketing at Walt Disney’s direct-to-consumer and international segment, announced her departure after a 34-year career. She cited the integration of 21st Century Fox and the rapid industry changes as factors in her decision. Marinelli oversaw significant operations including the distribution of Disney's film and TV programming and spearheaded the development of Movies Anywhere.

title: Commentary: Beyond Meat can’t save Blue Apron
summary: This article argues that while Beyond Meat and Blue Apron's partnership is a good idea for product exposure and menu variety, it will not solve Blue Apron's fundamental business problems. The author contends that Blue Apron's subscription model doesn't suit many consumers and cooking is still seen as a hassle, with increasing competition from grocery prepared-food offerings and third-party delivery services. The piece suggests that Blue Apron needs to focus on initiatives like on-demand delivery to encourage existing customers to spend more, rather than relying on new recipes.

title: Great Deals On Jessica Alba’s Honest Beauty And Baby Products On Amazon Prime Day
summary: Jessica Alba's Honest Company is offering significant discounts on its beauty and baby products for Amazon Prime Day. Fans can get up to 20 percent off items like the Vitamin C Radiance Serum and the Gently Nourishing Face and Body Lotion, along with a vegan leather backpack that doubles as a diaper bag. The Honest Company, founded in 2011, focuses on eco-friendly and safe consumer products, and has expanded into beauty items while previously lobbying Congress for stricter chemical input testing.

title: Walmart CEO McMillon says the retailer has been playing ‘catch up’ in e-commerce
summary: Walmart CEO Doug McMillon admits the retail giant has been "playing catch up" in e-commerce, specifically against Amazon.com Inc. McMillon stated at Fortune's Brainstorm Tech conference that Walmart has been undergoing a transformation to meet evolving consumer shopping demands. This acknowledges the company's efforts to adjust and progress in the digital retail space after an initial lag.

title: Microsoft, AT&T sign cloud deal worth more than $2 billion
summary: Microsoft and AT&T have signed a multi-year cloud deal valued at over $2 billion, making Microsoft AT&T's "preferred" cloud vendor. AT&T will utilize Microsoft's Azure cloud service and Microsoft 365 for its workforce and will collaborate with Microsoft on edge computing for its 5G network. This agreement marks a significant shift for AT&T towards a "public cloud first" strategy and strengthens Microsoft's position in the competitive cloud services market.

title: Amazon: Prime Day sales were bigger than Black Friday and Cyber Monday combined
summary: Amazon announced that its 2019 Prime Day sales surpassed the combined sales of Black Friday and Cyber Monday 2018, with members purchasing 175 million items globally. This two-day event also marked the biggest two days ever for new Prime member signups. The article notes Prime Day's growing influence, attracting competing retail sales and drawing attention to Amazon's employee wages.

title: eBay Welcomes Pete Thompson as Chief Product Officer; Mazen Rawashdeh promoted to Chief Technology Officer
summary: eBay announced new leadership appointments, welcoming Pete Thompson as Senior Vice President and Chief Product Officer and promoting Mazen Rawashdeh to Senior Vice President and Chief Technology Officer. Both executives will report to President and CEO Devin Wenig, with Thompson focusing on personalizing the shopping experience and Rawashdeh leading platform engineering and architecture. Additionally, Scott Gaffney joins as VP, Search Engineering, and Steve Metz returns as VP, Product Analytics, further strengthening eBay's leadership in product and technology.

title: Etsy to acquire music gear marketplace Reverb for $275M
summary: Etsy announced its definitive agreement to acquire Reverb Holdings, a musical instrument marketplace, for $275 million in cash. Reverb will operate as a standalone business, and its founder, David Kalt, will step down as CEO. The acquisition aims to leverage synergies between the two companies, with Etsy's CFO Rachel Glaser highlighting Reverb's similar business model and strong brand in a large market.

title: Target’s Small-Format Stores Are Its Biggest Weapon Against Amazon and Walmart
summary: Target's strategy of opening smaller-format stores in urban areas and college campuses is proving highly successful in its competition against Amazon and Walmart. These tailored stores, which are Target's most productive, are integrated into a strong delivery network, offering convenience like same-day delivery via Shipt, and bolstering customer loyalty and financial performance. This approach leverages Target's brand appeal and proximity to customers, resulting in significant growth in sales and stock performance.

title: Amazon, Realogy team up to help you buy your next house and get free stuff in the process
summary: Amazon and Realogy Holdings Corp. have launched "TurnKey," a new platform designed to streamline the home-buying process and offer incentives. The program connects homebuyers with local Realogy-affiliated agents and provides free Amazon smart home products and services worth $1,000 to $5,000, depending on the home's purchase price. This initiative aims to reduce stress for buyers while increasing sales for both companies and is available in 15 U.S. cities.

title: Kroger churns out new ice cream flavors to drive its sales
summary: Kroger is expanding its private label ice cream offerings, introducing exotic new flavors like Unicorn Swirl and Black Cherry Root Beer Float to boost sales and compete in the grocery market. These house brands are a significant part of Kroger's $22 billion private label business, providing both lower-cost and unique options to customers. The strategy is proving successful, with the Unicorn Swirl flavor quickly becoming a top seller, and overall ice cream innovations credited for generating $225 million in new sales this year.

title: Weis Markets Expands Weis 2 Go Program
summary: Weis Markets is expanding its Weis 2 Go online ordering service to 61 additional stores, bringing the total to 150 stores in seven states. This service allows customers to pick up groceries at designated locations or have them delivered to their homes, offering a seamless shopping experience through mobile ordering and online at WeisMarkets.com. For a limited time, the $4.95 curbside pick-up fee is waived, and customers can use coupons and Weis Preferred Shopper cards to save and earn rewards.

title: Apple Is Now the Most Valuable Brand Ever, Thanks to This 1 Thing. (The Good News Is You Can Totally Do It Too)
summary: Apple has become the most valuable brand globally, valued at $205 billion, largely due to its commitment to delighting customers beyond expectations. While the iPhone's success contributes, the core reason for its brand value lies in fostering positive feelings through every customer interaction. The article suggests that any business can achieve similar brand success by focusing on unexpected customer delight rather than just meeting expectations.

title: Off-White Voluntarily Dismisses Trademark Lawsuit Over Allegedly Infringing Bracelets
summary: Off-White has voluntarily dismissed its trademark infringement lawsuit against bracelet-maker Rastaclat, almost three months after filing the complaint. The lawsuit, centered on Rastaclat's use of red zip ties and quotation marks, was likely settled out of court, leading to the removal of the allegedly infringing products from Rastaclat's website and other retailers. This dismissal follows complications with Off-White's own trademark application for the red zip tie, which the USPTO preliminarily rejected on grounds of being confusingly similar to existing marks, functional, and lacking inherent distinctiveness.

title: Amazon’s run of record earnings comes to an end, and the stock is falling
summary: Amazon's streak of record quarterly profits has ended, with the company reporting a decline in second-quarter earnings despite strong sales growth. The e-commerce giant's stock fell in late trading as earnings of $2.6 billion, or $5.22 a share, missed analysts' estimates of $5.56 a share. Revenue, however, exceeded expectations, reaching $63.4 billion.

title: Report: Amazon Web Services Expands in Herndon
summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) is expanding its presence in Northern Virginia by leasing 13820 Sunrise Valley Drive in Herndon, adding to its significant footprint in the region. This expansion comes as AWS continues to pursue major federal government contracts, including the Department of Defense's $10 billion JEDI cloud contract. The company has leased close to 852,800 square feet in Northern Virginia, cementing its status as one of the fastest-growing tenants.

title: Louis Theroux leaving BBC to form production company; Netflix and Amazon circling (exclusive)
summary: Documentary filmmaker Louis Theroux is reportedly forming an independent production company after his current deal with the BBC ends, leading to a bidding war between Amazon and Netflix for a production deal. Theroux, who is collaborating with BBC Studios executive Arron Fellows on the new venture, is also considering continuing to make documentaries for the BBC in an independent capacity. His new company is expected to enter the podcast space alongside film production.

title: Capital One Data Breach Compromises Data of Over 100 Million (Published 2019)
summary: Capital One experienced one of the largest bank data thefts, compromising the personal data of over 100 million people. A software engineer, Paige Thompson, was arrested and charged with computer fraud and abuse after boasting about the hacking online. Thompson, a former Amazon Web Services employee, left an extensive digital trail that led to her identification and arrest.

title: FOX NFL Thursday Adds Another Hall of Famer to Star-Studded Lineup
summary: Tony Gonzalez, Class of 2019 Pro Football Hall of Famer, is joining the FOX NFL THURSDAY pregame show for the NFL's 100th season, starting September 26th. He will appear regularly alongside Michael Strahan, Terry Bradshaw, and Howie Long, with Strahan hosting the show. FOX Thursday Night Football games will be available on Amazon Prime Video, Twitch, and various NFL and FOX digital properties.

title: No more cardboard boxes? 3M invents an ingenious new way to ship products
summary: 3M has introduced Flex & Seal Shipping Roll, a new packaging material designed to replace cardboard boxes for items under 3 pounds. This innovation aims to reduce packing time, material waste, and shipping space by 50%, offering a self-sealing, tear- and water-resistant alternative for e-commerce shipments. While it offers efficiency and tamper protection, its recyclability currently requires specialized retail drop-offs, a challenge 3M is working to address.

title: As rural India develops taste for chocolate, Mondelez extends its reach
summary: Mondelez is significantly expanding its reach into rural India to capitalize on the growing taste for chocolate, driven by rising disposable incomes and a recent tax cut. The company is investing heavily in distribution networks, including refrigerated trucks and a database to track sales, aiming to reach up to 100,000 villages in the next three years. This strategic move aims to solidify Mondelez's dominant position in the burgeoning Indian confectionery market against competitors like Nestle SA and Hershey Co.

title: Africa’s Amazon Looks to Solve Addresses Problem With Vivo Tieup
summary: Jumia Technologies AG, often called Africa's Amazon, is partnering with Vivo Energy Plc to address the challenge of a lack of formal addresses for deliveries in less developed parts of Africa. Vivo Energy's 2,100+ Shell and Engen-branded service stations will serve as pick-up points for Jumia-bought goods, where customers can also pay. This collaboration aims to expand Jumia's reach, especially in remote areas, and boost Vivo's non-fuels business.

title: Gartner Says Worldwide IaaS Public Cloud Services Market Grew 31.3% in 2018
summary: The worldwide Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) market experienced significant growth in 2018, increasing by 31.3% to reach $32.4 billion. Amazon maintained its position as the leading vendor, followed by Microsoft, Alibaba, Google, and IBM, indicating a consolidation trend favoring major providers who can invest heavily in scalable data center infrastructure and offer a rich feature set.

title: Capital One Data Breach Impacts 106 Million Customers
summary: Capital One announced a massive data breach affecting 106 million customers and applicants in the U.S. and Canada, exposing personal details like names, social security numbers, and income. The alleged hacker, a former Amazon Web Services employee, has been arrested. Capital One is offering free credit monitoring and identity protection to those impacted, advising customers to monitor their accounts for suspicious activity.

title: Capital One Breach Shows a Bank Hacker Needs Just One Gap to Wreak Havoc (Published 2019)
summary: The Capital One data breach, which exposed the personal information of over 100 million people, highlights how a single vulnerability can be exploited by hackers despite robust cybersecurity measures. A former Amazon software engineer, Paige Thompson, allegedly gained access to Capital One's network through a "configuration vulnerability." This incident underscores the ongoing challenge financial institutions face in defending against persistent cyberattacks, needing only one lapse in security to succeed.

title: Paige Thompson, Suspect in Capital One Data Breach, Left a Trail Online (Published 2019)
summary: Paige Thompson, a 33-year-old software developer, was arrested for allegedly obtaining the personal data of over 100 million people from Capital One. Her extensive online presence, including social media posts and activity on developer platforms, created a digital trail that helped authorities track her down. Thompson had a history of software engineering jobs, including at Amazon Web Services.

title: About one million Canadian social insurance numbers compromised in Capital One data breach
summary: A massive data hack at Capital One Financial Corp. compromised the personal data of roughly six million Canadians and exposed one million social insurance numbers, making it one of Canada's largest security breaches. The incident, which also affected 100 million U.S. clients, led to the arrest of alleged hacker Paige A. Thompson. Capital One is notifying affected individuals and offering free credit monitoring and identity theft insurance.

title: Tractor Supply’s BOPIS strategy pays off in rural communities
summary: Tractor Supply's buy-online-pickup-in-store (BOPIS) strategy is proving highly successful in rural communities, with over 70% of online orders fulfilled in-store. This approach helps the company save on supply chain costs and boosts sales, particularly as rural customers often face challenges with fast and affordable last-mile delivery options. The strategy also positions Tractor Supply to compete effectively with e-commerce giants like Amazon in less densely populated areas.

title: Capital One shares dive after data breach affecting 100 million
summary: Capital One shares fell after the company disclosed a data breach affecting 100 million individuals, compromising Social Security numbers and bank account numbers for some customers. Analysts express concern over potential reputational damage and regulatory actions, with initial cost estimates for Capital One ranging from $100 million to $150 million. The FBI arrested a former Amazon Web Services employee in connection with the breach.

title: Former Amazon worker is accused in cloud hack of Capital One
summary: A former Amazon Web Services employee, Paige A. Thompson, has been accused of illegally accessing data from approximately 100 million U.S. Capital One customers and 6 million Canadian customers. The breach occurred due to a misconfigured firewall, Capital One stated, and the stolen data includes personal information, Social Security numbers, and bank account numbers. Capital One's stock fell following the announcement, and Thompson faces charges of computer fraud.

title: Capital One Data Theft Impacts 106M People
summary: Federal prosecutors charged a Seattle woman, Paige A. Thompson, with stealing data from over 100 million Capital One credit applications, impacting 106 million people in the U.S. and Canada. The breach exposed names, addresses, dates of birth, incomes, approximately 140,000 Social Security numbers, and 80,000 bank account numbers, although Capital One stated no credit card numbers or login credentials were compromised. The incident highlights misconfiguration issues in cloud platforms and the vulnerability of personal data, with Thompson allegedly discussing her activities on social media.

title: Capital One hack snags data on 106 million people — including 6 million in Canada
summary: A security breach at Capital One Financial compromised the personal information of about 106 million people, including 6 million in Canada, with some Social Security and bank account numbers obtained. The alleged hacker, Paige A. Thompson, was charged with computer fraud and abuse after federal agents tracked her online. Capital One's stock dipped six percent following the news, and the company plans to offer free credit monitoring to those affected by what is considered one of the largest security breaches of a major U.S. financial institution on record.

title: Capital One Reports Data Breach Affecting 100 Million Customers, Applicants
summary: Capital One announced a data breach impacting roughly 106 million customers and applicants. A former Amazon Web Services employee, Paige A. Thompson, was arrested in connection with the hack, which involved accessing data stored on Amazon's cloud service by breaching a Capital One firewall. Capital One is the fifth-largest U.S. credit-card issuer.

title: Capital One Reports Data Breach Affecting 100 Million Customers, Applicants
summary: Capital One Financial Corp., the fifth-largest U.S. credit-card issuer, reported a data breach affecting approximately 106 million customers and applicants. A former Amazon Web Services employee, Paige A. Thompson, has been arrested in connection with the hack. The incident is considered one of the largest-ever data breaches for a major bank.

title: Capital One Reports Data Breach Affecting 100 Million Customers, Applicants
summary: Capital One Financial Corp. announced a data breach affecting approximately 106 million credit-card customers and applicants, making it one of the largest data breaches for a major bank. A former Amazon Web Services employee, Paige A. Thompson, has been arrested in connection with the hack. She is accused of bypassing Capital One's firewall to access customer data stored on Amazon's cloud service.

title: A hacker gained access to 100 million Capital One credit card applications and accounts
summary: A hacker gained access to over 100 million Capital One customer accounts and credit card applications, exposing sensitive personal and financial data. The suspect, Paige Thompson, a former Amazon Web Services software engineer, was arrested and accused of exploiting a misconfigured web application firewall. Capital One estimates the breach will cost between $100 million and $150 million and is offering free credit monitoring to affected individuals.

title: Netflix is not a tech company
summary: Benedict Evans argues that Netflix, despite its reliance on technology, is fundamentally a TV company, much like Sky was in its time. He uses "technology as a crowbar" as a metaphor to explain how companies leverage tech to disrupt traditional industries, but their core business remains within that industry. The article emphasizes that for Netflix, the critical questions are "TV questions" related to content, rights, and industry dynamics, rather than "tech questions" typical of Silicon Valley.

title: Capital One touted the data cloud’s safety. Then a hacker breached it
summary: Capital One, a prominent advocate for cloud-based data storage, experienced a significant data breach affecting over 100 million customers. The incident, which involved a former Amazon Web Services employee exploiting a misconfigured firewall, has raised concerns about the security of financial data in the cloud despite Capital One's assertions of its safety and benefits. The breach is expected to cost Capital One between $100 million and $150 million, primarily for credit monitoring and legal support.

title: The Capital One breach was preventable, experts say. Here’s what to do now.
summary: Cybersecurity experts suggest that the Capital One data breach, which exposed over 100 million people's personal information, was preventable due to a misconfigured firewall. Former Seattle software engineer Paige Thompson was arrested after boasting about the data theft, which Capital One estimates will cost between $100 million and $150 million. The incident highlights concerns about cloud security, human error, and the transparency of companies in communicating breaches to affected customers.
